Simulated engagement states and trajectories over a study programme

Source: R/data.R
engagement_momentum.Rd

engagement_momentum is a simulated dataset of student engagement across the courses of a study programme. Each row represents one student's enrolment in one course, with courses ordered within students. In every course a student is in one of three engagement states (active, average or disengaged), measured by five activity indicators standardized within course; over the programme each student follows one of three trajectories (engaged, fluctuating or mostly disengaged). Each course also has a grade.

The design follows the study of engagement dynamics by López-Pernas and Saqr (2024): engaged students show momentum, an active course tending to be followed by another, and mostly disengaged students show inertia, a disengaged course tending to be followed by another. The parameter values are illustrative choices that reproduce these patterns; they are not estimates from that study.

Usage

engagement_momentum

Format

A data frame with 1310 rows (106 students, 32 courses, one row per student and course, 10 to 15 enrolments each, no missing values) and 12 columns:

student

Integer student identifier, 1 to 106. The nesting unit; pass it as id.

course

Integer course identifier, 1 to 32.

sequence

Integer position of the course in the student's programme; pass it as time.

browse

Numeric, course page views, standardized within course.

lectures

Numeric, lecture views, standardized within course.

forum_read

Numeric, forum posts read, standardized within course.

forum_post

Numeric, forum posts written, standardized within course.

active_days

Numeric, days with online activity, standardized within course.

grade

Numeric course grade, standardized over the data.

previous_grade

Numeric grade of the previous course (an entry grade at the first course), standardized over the data.

state

Factor, the generating engagement state: "active", "average" or "disengaged".

trajectory

Factor, the generating trajectory, constant within student: "engaged", "fluctuating" or "mostly_disengaged".

Source

Simulated by data-raw/engagement-momentum.R, following the design of López-Pernas, S., & Saqr, M. (2024). How the dynamics of engagement explain the momentum of achievement and the inertia of disengagement: A complex systems theory approach. Computers in Human Behavior, 153, 108126. doi:10.1016/j.chb.2023.108126

Details

Students take 10 to 15 courses, ordered by sequence. Use id = "student" for the nesting structure and time = "sequence" for occasion order. The trajectories differ both in the mix of states they visit, which multilpa() recovers as group classes, and in their transitions between states, which lta() recovers. The five indicators are drawn independently within a state, so the default diagonal covariance structure is the generating one; unlike course_engagement, the data contain no within-state dependence between indicators. The grade of each course depends on its engagement state and on the previous grade.

Examples

descriptives(engagement_momentum,
             vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post",
                      "active_days"),
             id = "student")
#>      variable    n n_missing          mean        sd   min  max n_distinct
#> 1      browse 1310         0 -8.396947e-05 0.9880070 -2.74 2.46        401
#> 2    lectures 1310         0 -5.343511e-05 0.9881515 -2.79 2.96        399
#> 3  forum_read 1310         0 -9.923664e-05 0.9880624 -2.46 2.80        386
#> 4  forum_post 1310         0  6.106870e-05 0.9879953 -2.54 3.06        395
#> 5 active_days 1310         0 -9.160305e-05 0.9880802 -2.62 2.83        392
#>   n_groups sd_within sd_between       icc
#> 1      106 0.8657215  0.5343503 0.2338112
#> 2      106 0.8847087  0.5087785 0.1998268
#> 3      106 0.8479255  0.5624311 0.2652751
#> 4      106 0.8781614  0.5179887 0.2114586
#> 5      106 0.8494755  0.5602438 0.2625956
fit <- multilpa(engagement_momentum,
                vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post",
                         "active_days"),
                id = "student", n_profiles = 3, n_group_classes = 3,
                n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
get_results(fit, what = "profile_probabilities")
#>   group_class profile probability group_class_probability
#> 1           1       1  0.85961489               0.1965273
#> 2           1       2  0.12216741               0.1965273
#> 3           1       3  0.01821770               0.1965273
#> 4           2       1  0.32321874               0.4461940
#> 5           2       2  0.34957303               0.4461940
#> 6           2       3  0.32720823               0.4461940
#> 7           3       1  0.06602054               0.3572788
#> 8           3       2  0.18266256               0.3572788
#> 9           3       3  0.75131689               0.3572788
# Compare the fitted classes with the generating states and trajectories.
get_results(fit, what = "assignments", data = engagement_momentum,
            truth = c("state", "trajectory"))
#>     assignment class      truth             value   n proportion
#> 1      profile     1      state            active   0 0.00000000

#> 6      profile     3      state           average  39 0.12074303
#> 7      profile     1      state        disengaged 415 0.94748858

#> 9      profile     3      state        disengaged   0 0.00000000
